root.label: Operator overloading
root.note: An operator expression on class or enum operands calls a function chosen by overload resolution.

children.label: What can be overloaded
children.note: Nearly every operator, but never its precedence, associativity or arity.

children.label: Not overloadable
children.note: ::, ., .*, ?:, sizeof, alignof, typeid and noexcept.

children.label: Overloadable surprises
children.note: ->*, the comma, co_await, new, delete and conversion functions can all be overloaded.

children.label: Class or enum operand
children.note: A non-member operator needs a parameter of class or enumeration type, so int + int stays built-in.

children.label: Member or non-member
children.note: Some operators must be members; symmetric ones are better as non-members.

children.label: Must be members
children.note: =, (), [] and -> can only be member functions.

children.label: Left operand
children.note: A member never converts its left operand, so 2 + v fails when only v + 2 is a member.

children.label: Hidden friends
children.note: Friends defined in the class get symmetric conversions and are found only by ADL.

children.label: Call, subscript, arrow
children.note: The three object-bound forms with special rules.

children.label: operator()
children.note: Any arity and default arguments; may be static since C++23.

children.label: Multidimensional []
children.note: Since C++23 operator[] takes any number of parameters, may be static, and may have defaults.

children.label: Comma in brackets
children.note: Built-in a[1, 2] is ill-formed in C++23; GCC still accepts it with a warning.

children.label: -> drill-down
children.note: x->m applies operator-> repeatedly until a raw pointer results.

children.label: Increment and decrement
children.note: Prefix and postfix share a token and differ by a dummy parameter.

children.label: Dummy int
children.note: operator++(int) is postfix; x++ calls it with the argument 0.

children.label: Return conventions
children.note: Prefix returns *this by reference, postfix returns the old value by copy.

children.label: Lost guarantees
children.note: Overloads are function calls, so built-in evaluation rules do not all survive.

children.label: No short-circuit
children.note: Overloaded &&, || and comma always evaluate both operands.

children.label: C++17 sequencing
children.note: Operands of an overloaded operator follow the built-in operator's sequencing order.

children.label: Unary &
children.note: Can be overloaded, so generic code uses std::addressof.

children.label: new and delete
children.note: Allocation functions that supply storage; the new expression still constructs the object.

children.label: User-defined literals
children.note: operator""_suffix gives a literal suffix a meaning.

children.label: Underscore suffixes
children.note: Suffixes without a leading underscore are reserved for the standard library.

children.label: Fixed parameter lists
children.note: Integer literals want unsigned long long, floating ones long double, else raw const char* or a template.

children.label: No conversions
children.note: With only a long double operator, 12_km is ill-formed.

children.label: Spaced form deprecated
children.note: C++23 deprecates operator"" _x with a space before the suffix.
